subject: Acme Health: sudden p95/p99 regressions impacting inference — immediate action plan
messages:
From: Sara Patel <sara@acme-health.com>
To: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@acme-health.com
Date: 2027-04-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Sharp rise in p95/p99 latency this morning — urgent

Ethan,

We started seeing a big jump in tail latency around 08:40 PST — p95 jumped from ~240ms to >1.2s and p99 above 2.5s. A small but growing percentage of requests are timing out (504) for our production API key. This is causing user-facing errors in our clinical intake flow.

We haven't changed our traffic pattern intentionally; the only change on our side was a rollout of a new client-side retry that started at 07:55, but traffic volume is within our normal range. Can you confirm whether anything changed on Redwood's side or if there is capacity pressure? We need a timeline and a workaround.

-Sara
VP Engineering, Acme Health

---

From: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara@acme-health.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-21T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sharp rise in p95/p99 latency this morning — urgent

Hi Sara — sorry you're seeing this. We're investigating now and I've looped in Product Ops and Engineering. Quick questions to help triage:

- Which model/route are you hitting (model id or route name)?
- Do you have any request traces or sample request_ids we can look up?

Immediate steps: I'll ask the on-call to pull service metrics and look for queue depth / batching anomalies; we'll aim to escalate to execs within the hour if this is platform-related.

I'll follow up in the thread within 20–30 minutes with an initial update.

—Ethan
Account Lead, Redwood Inference

---

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-21T09:34:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Sharp rise in p95/p99 latency this morning — urgent

Quick summary from the runtime team:

- Observed correlated spike in request queue depth on the shared hosted pool beginning ~08:35 PST.
- Batching metrics show a sudden increase in batch sizes and per-batch preparation time for the seq-length distribution Acme is sending.
- Autoscaler reports no immediate capacity shortage, but there is elevated tail latency driven by longer waiting times in the request queue (continuous batching backlog).

Preliminary hypothesis: a change in client-side behavior (retries + slightly larger payloads) has increased inter-arrival variance; our batching window widened to try and fill larger batches, which increased queue wait time for short requests and pushed p95/p99 up.

Action items (internal):
- Karthik and I will snapshot queue and batching histograms and correlate with Acme's request_ids.
- Marissa to prepare a canary rollback of the last heuristic tweak to the batching window for the affected pool.
- Ethan to coordinate customer comms and request sample traces from Acme.

Dylan (Runtime SRE)

---

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-21T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Sharp rise in p95/p99 latency this morning — urgent

Findings so far (10:00 snapshot):

- Batch window heuristic change deployed 2027-04-21T07:50 across the hosted pool: increased max batching window from 8ms -> 18ms to improve throughput for long sequences. This aligns with the timing.
- Acme's traffic pattern has many short-sequence requests (median token length ~18) but with intermittent bursts caused by the client retry rollout. The increased max window means short requests now wait longer to reach target batch sizes.
- Queue depth rose from typical 30–45 to 160–220 in the affected region pool for ~35 minutes.
- Error rate increase is downstream timeouts at the API gateway during the queue-wait window, not model execution failures.

Recommendation (immediate):
- Roll back the batching window heuristic for the hosted pool serving Acme to 8ms (canary for 10% traffic in 15 minutes).
- Add a short-term per-customer override to favor latency-sensitive keys (reduce batching window).

I'll attach the histograms and timeline (see attachments).

Karthik (Principal Ops Engineer)
messages_addendum:

From: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara@acme-health.com>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@acme-health.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-21T10:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sharp rise in p95/p99 latency this morning — immediate mitigations underway

Sara / Tom — thanks for the quick reply & sample request ids. Short update:

- We've identified a batching policy change that coincides with the timing you reported. The runtime team is launching a canary rollback to the previous batching window for 10% of your traffic right now.
- If the canary shows p95 improvement within 10–15 minutes, we will extend the rollback to 100% of your traffic.
- As a protective measure, we're enabling a per-key low-latency override for your production API key to minimize queueing while we finish the rollout.

Expected timeline: canary -> 10–15m, expansion -> +15m, monitoring -> ongoing. I'll post another update when we have canary metrics.

—Ethan

-Sara

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-21T10:55:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Sharp rise in p95/p99 latency this morning — immediate mitigations underway

Canary results at 10:52:

- Canary (10% traffic) p95 dropped from 1.18s -> 0.26s within 6 minutes of rollback. p99 showed similar improvement.
- Overall error rate for Acme keys decreased from 1.9% -> 0.3% in the canary segment.
- We are promoting rollback to 100% at 10:58 and enabling the per-key low-latency override immediately.

Next steps (internal):
- Post-mortem to capture why the batching heuristic change didn't account for short-sequence, high-variance clients.
- Short-term: create per-tenant latency overrides and an alert when queue depth for a pool crosses 120.
- Product: revisit the default batching window policy and add region-specific profiles.

Marissa (Prod Ops)

---

From: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara@acme-health.com>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@acme-health.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-21T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Final update: rollback complete, monitoring and exec summary

Sara / Tom — final update for today:

- Rollback to previous batching window completed 11:05 PST; per-key override enacted for your production key.
- Measured improvement: p95 returned to ~240–280ms baseline; p99 under 700ms during post-rollout monitoring period.
- Root cause (preliminary): an across-the-board batching window increase to improve throughput for long sequences unintentionally penalized short, latency-sensitive clients when combined with sudden retry-driven bursts.

We're preparing a brief exec summary and a proposed product change set:
- Immediate: per-tenant latency overrides and a queue-depth alert threshold.
- Near-term: adaptive batching heuristics that consider token-length distribution + recent inter-arrival variance.
- Follow-up: joint post-mortem with Acme next week — propose Wed 2027-04-28 09:00 PST.

If you'd like a quick sync now to walk through the telemetry, I'm available; otherwise we'll send the exec notes + access to the timeline folder.

Thanks again for the patience and the rapid sample traces — that helped reduce time-to-resolution.

—Ethan
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
